topic: Your ML Model Works in Staging. Production Says No.
postText:
Last month a model passed every offline test with 94% accuracy. We deployed it behind a feature flag. Within hours, live predictions degraded on 30% of requests. Nobody changed the model. The world changed around it.

This is the gap most ML teams ignore: staging environments are a lie. Your test set is frozen. Production traffic is a river. Feature distributions shift, upstream services change formats, and suddenly your carefully tuned model is confidently wrong.

The fix is not "better testing." It's architectural:

1. Shadow deploy first. Mirror real traffic to the new model in parallel. Log predictions. Compare against the incumbent. Zero user exposure, full production signal.

2. Enforce a feature parity contract. Assert that train-time and serve-time feature pipelines produce identical outputs. Fail the deploy on drift, not on a dashboard nobody watches.

3. Automate quality gates. Block model promotion when live accuracy or p95 latency crosses thresholds. Make rollback a one-command operation, not a 3 AM incident call.

In healthcare IT, a degraded prediction isn't a metric. It's a triage recommendation someone trusts. We learned to treat model deployment like any other distributed system change: observable, reversible, gated.

Question for the engineers here: when you ship a model, what is your actual rollback trigger? A metric threshold, a human judgment call, or a page at 3 AM?

If this resonated, drop your experience in the comments, Like if it helped, and Share it with a teammate who still trusts their staging environment. Follow @pengikut for more production architecture lessons.

transcription:
Your model passed every offline test. Then production traffic hit.
30% of predictions degraded. Nobody changed the model.
Staging is a frozen test set. Production is a river.
Shadow deploy: mirror real traffic, compare outputs, zero user impact.
Enforce feature parity. Automate quality gates. Make rollback one command.
Offline metrics prove nothing. Shadow traffic is the only honest test.
